support.metaDescription: Answers to common questions about Bibi: orders, payments, run sheets, your team and your subscription.
support.title: How can we help?
support.lead: Short answers to the questions we get most often. Can't find what you're looking for? Get in touch and we'll help you.

whatIsBibi.question: What is Bibi?
whatIsBibi.answer:
Bibi is a booking system for venues that sell meetings, conferences, food and drink. Your staff use it to create orders, keep track of rooms and send run sheets to the kitchen and other teams.
Your customers never need to log in. They only see the page where they pay.

startTrial.question: How do I get started?
startTrial.answer:
Click Try for free on our front page, create your account and name your organization. You get 14 days free with everything included.
When the trial ends, an admin adds a payment method to keep using Bibi.

exampleOrders.question: What are the example orders on my board?
exampleOrders.answer:
When you finish setting up Bibi, we add three example orders so your board isn't empty: a meeting, a conference and a dinner. They all belong to the customer Example Company Ltd and use the types you chose.
Click around in them, edit them and move them as you like.
When you're done, open Example Company Ltd under Customers, archive the contact person Anna Example, then archive the customer with Also archive all orders for this customer ticked.

itemGroups.question: How do I sort my items into groups like Spaces and Food?
itemGroups.answer:
Go to Settings, open Types and find Groups. Create a group, then open a type and pick its group. You can rename, reorder and archive groups there.
Items then shows one tab per group, so rooms, food and extras are no longer mixed in one list.
When you set up Bibi, we create Spaces, Food & drink and Extras for you.

venueItems.question: How do I see what a venue has?
venueItems.answer:
Open Venues and pick a venue. Under Items you see how many items of each type it has, with the first few names.
Click a type to see all of those items, or Show all items to see everything at the venue.

pluralName.question: Where do I set what a type is called in plural?
pluralName.answer:
Go to Settings, open Types and pick a type. Fill in Plural name, for example Conference rooms, and click Save.
Bibi uses it where several items are listed together, like the items summary on a venue. Left empty, the type's own name is used.

inviteColleagues.question: How do I invite my colleagues?
inviteColleagues.answer:
Go to Administration → Members and invite them by email. They get a link that takes them straight into your organization.
Ten seats are included in the subscription.

findSetting.question: Where do I find a setting?
findSetting.answer:
Press Cmd+K (Ctrl+K on Windows) to open the command bar and type what you are looking for, for example "time zone", "VAT" or "Stripe". Under **Settings**, choose a result to go straight to that part of the page.
You only see results for the parts you have access to.

signIn.question: How do I sign in?
signIn.answer:
Enter your email address and we send you a sign-in link. Open the link and you're in, no password to remember.
No email? Check your spam folder, or ask for a new link.

orders.title: Orders and payments
orders.description: Creating orders, holding rooms and getting paid.

createOrder.question: How do I create an order?
createOrder.answer:
Click Create order, pick the customer and add the lines: rooms, food, activities. You can also ask the assistant to create it for you.
For smaller meetings you don't need a quote first. Create the order and send the payment straight away.

customerValue.question: How much is a customer worth?
customerValue.answer:
Open Customers. The Value column shows how much each customer has been billed so far, including VAT.
An order counts once it has been invoiced, or once the customer has accepted its quote. Hover the question mark next to Value to see this explained.

createFromBoard.question: Can I create an order from the pipeline board?
createFromBoard.answer: Yes. At the bottom of the column where new orders start there is + Create order. It opens the same page as Create order in the menu, and the order lands in that first column.

holds.question: What is the difference between a soft and a hard hold?
holds.answer:
A soft hold reserves a room for a customer who hasn't decided yet. Others can see it, and it has an expiry date so the room doesn't stay blocked forever.
A hard hold blocks the room completely. Which statuses give a soft or a hard hold is set up by your admin.

customerPay.question: How does my customer pay?
customerPay.answer:
Send the customer a payment link from the order. They open it and choose how to pay, by card or Swish, without creating an account.
Which methods they see depends on what your admin has connected. You can also send an invoice instead.

changeStatus.question: How do I move an order to the next step?
changeStatus.answer:
Change the status on the order page, or drag the order on the board. If a step needs something done first, Bibi tells you what is missing.
The steps themselves are set up by your admin.

refund.question: How do I refund a payment?
refund.answer:
Open the order, find the payment under **Payments** and choose **Refund**. Leave the amount empty to refund everything that is left, or type a smaller amount for a partial refund.
The money goes back the way the customer paid. The payment shows the refunded amount once the payment service confirms it. If the payment service has not confirmed a refund after 15 minutes, Bibi checks with it again by itself and sends the refund again if it never arrived.

paidTwice.question: What happens if a customer pays twice?
paidTwice.answer:
If a customer pays the same payment again, for example with both card and Swish, Bibi keeps the money and tells the people on the order with a notification that it was paid again.
Open the order, find the payment under **Payments** and choose **Refund** to send the extra back, or keep it as credit for the customer.

cancelPayment.question: Can I cancel a payment link I already sent?
cancelPayment.answer:
Yes, as long as it is not paid. Open the order, find the payment and choose **Cancel payment**.
The link stops working for the customer. If money still comes in, Bibi records it.

recordPayment.question: The customer paid by bank transfer. How do I record it?
recordPayment.answer:
Open the order and choose **Record payment** next to the quote, deposit or invoice the money was for. Enter the amount, the day it arrived and a note such as the reference.
The balance on the order updates at once.

creditNote.question: How do I credit an invoice?
creditNote.answer:
Open the order and choose **Credit** next to the sent invoice. Leave the amount empty to credit everything still due, or type a smaller amount, and add a reason.
Bibi creates a credit note that lowers what the customer owes. If the invoice was made in your accounting system, it is credited there too. Money already paid is given back with **Refund** on the payment.

voidInvoice.question: What happens when I void an invoice made in a payment service?
voidInvoice.answer:
Open the order and choose **Void** next to the invoice. Bibi voids it in the payment service too.
If the service says no, the invoice goes back to sent and you see why. If the service does not answer, the invoice shows that voiding is not confirmed yet, and Bibi tries again every 15 minutes until it is.

layouts.title: Rooms and layouts
layouts.description: Draw a room's floor plan and its layouts, with capacity and times.

drawLayout.question: How do I draw a layout for a room?
drawLayout.answer:
Open the room under Items and choose Layouts. Click Create layout, give it a name and say what it suits; an empty layout offers rows of chairs, a U-shape or a banquet for the number of people you type.
Drag furniture from the panel on the left onto the room, or click it to place it in the middle. Click Save when you are done.

severalLayouts.question: Can a room have more than one layout?
severalLayouts.answer:
Yes. A room has one floor plan and as many layouts as you furnish it in, for example Banquet 60 with round tables and Banquet 80 with long tables. Create layout can start from a copy of one you already have.
The item page shows every layout as a small drawing with its name, its capacity and what it suits. Delete a layout from the menu with three dots in the layout.

layoutDetails.question: How do I set a layout's capacity and setup time?
layoutDetails.answer:
Open the layout, click the menu with three dots and choose Edit layout details. There you can change the name, write what the layout suits, type a capacity and say how many minutes it takes to set up before and tear down after a booking.
Leave a time empty to use the room's own, then click Save.

tableChairs.question: How do I change a table's size or where the chairs are?
tableChairs.answer:
Click the table. Above it you can set its size in centimetres and choose how many chairs go on each side, for example only on one long side, or one at each end.
Reset to the library's size and chairs puts the table back the way it is in your furniture.

capacity.question: How is a layout's capacity counted?
capacity.answer:
A layout's capacity is the number you type for it, or else the number of chairs in its drawing. Bibi warns when a booking has more guests than that.
For standing guests, or when you want another number, type a capacity under Edit layout details.

maxPeople.question: What is a room's people limit?
maxPeople.answer:
It is the most people the room may hold, for example because of fire safety and ventilation. You type it as Max number of people when you edit the room under Items.
It is a hard limit: a layout or a booking with more people than that is not saved, and you cannot lower the limit below a layout or a coming booking that needs more.

emergencyExit.question: How do I mark an emergency exit?
emergencyExit.answer:
Open the room under Items, choose Floor plan, click a door or window and switch on Emergency exit. The exit is drawn in green with a hatched area in front of it.
Furniture may not stand in that area: a layout with a chair or table there cannot be saved until you move it, and you cannot mark an exit that a layout already blocks.

floorPlan.question: Where do I put doors, windows and pillars?
floorPlan.answer:
Open the room under Items and choose Floor plan. Doors, windows, pillars and screens placed there show in every layout of the room, and Bibi warns if furniture stands where a door opens.
Doors and windows always sit on a wall: drag one and it follows the nearest wall. Click it to set its width and how far it opens.

roomShape.question: How do I draw a room that is not a rectangle?
roomShape.answer:
Open the room under Items and choose Floor plan. Drag a corner to move the walls, click the + in the middle of a wall to add a corner, and double-click a corner to delete it.
Each wall shows its length. Click Save when the shape is right; every layout of the room uses it. Use the menu with three dots to set the room's width and depth.

history.question: Where can I see who changed an item?
history.answer:
Open the item and look just under its title: it says when it was last edited and by whom. To see every change, click the three dots at the top right and choose View history.
A panel opens with who changed what and when. You only see this if you have access to the change history.

lists.title: Your own lists and run sheets
lists.description: Keep track of what each order needs, your way.

customLists.question: Can we keep track of our own things on an order, like diets, equipment or languages?
customLists.answer:
Yes. An admin creates your own lists under Administration → Lists, for anything you want to count: diets, technical equipment, accessibility, interpreting languages or something only your venue uses.
On the order you then enter counts against a list, for example 4 vegetarian or 2 projectors. No names or personal details needed.

matching.question: What does Bibi do with the counts?
matching.answer: Bibi matches them against your items and puts them on the right run sheet, so the kitchen, the technicians or the hosts see what they need to prepare.

runSheet.question: How do I send a run sheet to the kitchen?
runSheet.answer: Open the run sheet and send it to the person responsible, for example the head chef. If the order changes later, they get a new version and can see what changed.

export.question: Can I print or export a run sheet?
export.answer: Yes. Download it as PDF to print, or as CSV or JSON if someone needs the data in another system.

whatCanItDo.question: What can the assistant do?
whatCanItDo.answer: Almost anything you can do yourself in Bibi: find orders, create an order from an email, check which rooms are free or summarize the week. Write what you need in plain language.

approvals.question: Can the assistant change things without asking me?
approvals.answer: No. The assistant suggests a change and waits until you approve it. Nothing is saved before you say yes, and you can always see who made a change.

settings.question: Can I see and change settings in the chat?
settings.answer:
Yes. Ask the assistant, for example "Which time zone do we use?" or "How big is the deposit?", and the settings show as a card in the chat.
If you may change them, do it right in the card. The change is saved when you pick a new value or choose **Save**, and a notice shows that it is saving and then that it is saved. You only see settings you have access to.

team.title: Your team and access
team.description: Who can see and do what.

roles.question: What roles are there?
roles.answer:
There are three: member, manager and admin. Members do the daily work with orders, managers can also handle prices and the catalog, and admins manage settings, members and billing.
An admin can adjust what each person may do.

cantSee.question: Why can't I see a page or a button?
cantSee.answer: You probably don't have access to that part. Ask an admin in your organization to give you access under Administration → Members.

price.question: What does Bibi cost?
price.answer: 9 990 SEK a month excluding VAT, with 10 seats included. Extra seats cost 49 SEK a month each. Pay yearly and you get 10 % off.

afterTrial.question: What happens when the trial ends?
afterTrial.answer: After 14 days Bibi asks for payment before you can continue. Nothing you created is lost, it is all there when payment is in place.

manageBilling.question: Where do I find my invoices and change payment details?
manageBilling.answer: An admin finds them under Administration → Plan & billing.

integrations.title: Accounting and integrations
integrations.description: Connecting Bibi to the systems you already use.

fortnox.question: Can I connect Bibi to Fortnox?
fortnox.answer: Yes. An admin connects Fortnox under Administration → Integrations and signs in to Fortnox to approve the connection.

otherAccounting.question: We use another accounting system. What do we do?
otherAccounting.answer: Export your sales as an SIE file under Administration → Accounting. Most Swedish accounting systems can import it.

paymentMethods.question: Can I choose which service takes card, Swish and invoice payments?
paymentMethods.answer:
Yes. Go to Administration → Payments and pick a service for each payment method under **Payment methods**. Each choice saves right away.
**Automatic** uses the connected service that can take the method. Connect services first under Administration → Integrations.

swish.question: How do we connect Swish?
swish.answer:
You need Swish for merchants (Swish Handel) from your bank, with your Swish number and the certificate file (.p12) and its passphrase.
An admin opens Administration → Integrations, chooses **Connect** on Swish and fills in the three details. Bibi checks them with Swish before saving them.

visma.question: Can I connect Bibi to Visma eEkonomi?
visma.answer:
Yes. An admin chooses **Connect** on Visma eEkonomi under Administration → Integrations and signs in to Visma to approve the connection.
Then pick Visma eEkonomi for **Invoice** under Administration → Payments, and invoices are made there with payments mirrored back to Bibi. Card and Swish payments taken in Bibi on a Visma invoice are booked in Visma too.

contact.title: Still need help?
contact.body: Ask the assistant in Bibi, it knows your organization's setup. For questions about access, ask an admin in your organization.
contact.email: Email us at {email} and we'll get back to you.

support.guidesLead: Step-by-step guides to the main parts of Bibi.

introduction.title: Introduction
introduction.lead: Bibi is a booking system for conferences, food and drink at venues without a hotel system. Your staff use it. Your guests and customers never log in.
introduction.body:
# What Bibi is for

Bibi helps venue staff handle orders from the first contact to the finished event. It is built for places such as experience centres, museums, conference estates, manor houses and restaurants with private rooms.

The people who use it are your sales staff, coordinators, kitchen leads and administrators. Customers and guests never use the app. The only page a customer sees is the payment page you send them.

# What you can do

- **Follow every request in one place.** An order is created as soon as a customer asks, and moves through your own statuses until it is done or lost. See [Orders](/support/orders).
- **Plan the program.** Add lines to an order, with the room, the layout and the number of people. Rooms cannot be double booked.
- **Record needs as counts.** For example "Gluten x 3" or "Wheelchair x 2", never tied to a named person. See [Needs and run sheets](/support/needs-and-run-sheets).
- **Send run sheets to the people who need them.** A run sheet is a versioned compilation, for example a kitchen order, and Bibi marks what changed since the last version you sent.
- **Take payment.** Customers pay a link or an invoice, and the money goes straight to your own Stripe account. See [Payments](/support/payments).
- **Ask the assistant.** You can do most of this by chatting. The assistant proposes changes and you approve them. See [The assistant](/support/assistant).

# Your organization sets the vocabulary

Bibi does not decide what you call things. Each organization defines its own types, fields, lists, statuses, run sheets and responsibilities. A conference estate may have "Conference room" and "Dish". A museum may have "Gallery" and "Guided tour". This guide uses examples such as allergens and kitchen orders, but they are examples only. What you see in your own account depends on how it is set up. See [Configuration](/support/configuration).

# Where to start

1. Read [Getting started](/support/getting-started) to sign in and find your way around.
2. If you are an administrator, set up your types, lists and statuses first.
3. Create an order, either from Orders or by asking the assistant.

# For developers

If you want to connect your own systems, see the [developer documentation](/developers).

getting-started.title: Getting started
getting-started.lead: Sign in, pick your organization and learn where things are in the menu.
getting-started.body:
# Sign in

1. Open Bibi and choose **Sign in**. Enter your email address and choose **Send sign-in link**, then open the link in the email. There is no password.
2. If you are new, choose **Create account**, enter your name and email address, and open the link we send you.
3. If a colleague invited you, open the link in the invitation email, sign in with the invited email address and choose **Accept invitation**.

If you belong to several organizations, you land on **Choose organization**. Pick one, or choose **Create organization** to start a new one. You can switch later from the user menu.

# The start page is the assistant

After you sign in you land on a chat. This is the assistant, and it is the quickest way to find things or make a change. Choose **Create chat** to start over. Earlier conversations are listed in the left menu under **Assistant**. See [The assistant](/support/assistant).

# The left menu

The menu has three parts.

- **Assistant** at the top: the home page, **Create chat** and your recent conversations.
- **Work**: **Orders** and **Customers**.
- **Catalog**: **Items** and **Venues**.

At the bottom left you find **Administration** (only for admins) and your user menu. The user menu holds theme (light, dark or system), language (Swedish or English), switching organization, **My skills** and **Sign out**.

At the top right there is a command bar. Press Cmd+K (Ctrl+K on Windows) to search or jump to a page. To the left of it a breadcrumb shows where you are. The assistant lives on the start page.

# A first checklist

If your organization is new and you are an administrator, work through this list. Each step links to a page with details.

1. Create your types under **Administration, Types**, or import a template. See [Configuration](/support/configuration).
2. Add your lists, for example allergens, under **Administration, Lists**.
3. Review your statuses under **Administration, Order flow**.
4. Create a venue, then add your rooms and other items. See [Items and venues](/support/items-and-venues).
5. Invite your colleagues under **Administration, Members**. See [Members and roles](/support/members-and-roles).
6. Connect Stripe under **Administration, Payments** if you want customers to pay online. See [Payments](/support/payments).
7. Add a customer, then create an order. See [Orders](/support/orders).

If you are not an administrator, you will not see **Administration**. Ask an administrator in your organization to set up what you need.

assistant.title: The assistant
assistant.lead: The assistant answers questions and prepares changes for you. It never changes anything until you approve.
assistant.body:
# What it can do

The assistant works as you. It can only see and do what your own role allows, in your own organization. Use it to:

- find orders, customers, items and venues
- show an order, a run sheet or a list of occupied rooms
- prepare a change, for example creating a customer or moving a line

Try questions such as "Show all venues", "Find bookable items that fit 50 people" or "Which skills are available?".

# Where to find it

- On the start page it fills the screen. Choose **Create chat** for a fresh conversation.
- It only lives on the start page. A question asked from the command bar (Cmd+K) takes you there.
- Your recent conversations are listed in the left menu under **Assistant**. You can rename or archive a conversation from its menu.
- On a phone the menu opens as a drawer from the top bar.

# Approving changes

The assistant never saves a change by itself. When it wants to change something it shows an **Approve action** card that lists exactly what will happen.

1. Read the card. Check the fields and values.
2. Choose **Approve** to carry it out, or **Reject** to drop it.
3. A proposal expires after a short time. If you see **The proposal has expired**, ask again.

Every change is recorded in the history of the order or customer. History shows whether the assistant proposed it and who approved it.

# Skills

A skill is a saved set of instructions that the assistant loads when it fits the task, for example "how we write a quote reply". There are three kinds: system skills that come with Bibi, organization skills shared by your administrators, and personal skills only you can see.

- Find organization skills and your own under **My skills** in the user menu.
- Choose **Create skill**, describe when it applies and what the assistant should do, then publish it.
- You can also import a SKILL.md file. It arrives as a draft.

# Good to know

- The assistant can be wrong. Check the approval card, not just the chat text.
- It uses the same rules as you do. If you cannot change something, neither can it.
- If the assistant is unavailable, an administrator at Bibi has not selected a model yet. The rest of the app works as usual.
- Developers can connect other tools to the same capabilities. See [MCP](/developers/mcp) and [Approvals](/developers/approvals).

orders.title: Orders
orders.lead: An order is one customer request, from the first contact to the finished event. This page shows how to create one, from who asks to Create, and how to move it through your statuses.
orders.body:
# Create an order

Open **Orders** and choose **Create order**. The page is one screen with steps in order. Only the open step takes input. A finished step collapses to one line with **Change**, which reopens it and keeps the answers after it. Nothing is saved until **Create order**, except a customer or contact you create in step 1.

1. **Who**: search for the customer by name. The five most recent customers show while the box is empty. If the customer is new, choose **New customer** and give the name, type, and a contact name and email. Bibi first checks for a similar customer and says "looks like ..." with **Use ...** or **No, it is a new customer**, so you do not create a duplicate. A contact person is required: the customer's only contact is used, you pick when there are several, and a customer without one asks you to add one.
2. **When and how many**: the date, from and to (in your organization's time zone) and the estimated number of guests.
3. **Package or one-off**: every package is grouped by what is free at that time. **Available** packages fit the time and the guest range. **Not available then** packages clash with another booking. **Outside your time or guest range** packages are made for other guest numbers or run past your end time. Each card shows its guest range and notes such as "Available" or "1 clash with other bookings". **One-off** builds the booking line by line.
4. **Review the booking** (or build it, for a one-off): the lines with their time, quantity and availability, a calendar for the day, notes on the booking, and **Create order**.

# Packages and the follow-up dialog

A package is a ready-made set of lines for a small meeting, with the guest range it is made for. Staff create it once and use it for every similar request. When you pick a package that needs a decision, a dialog asks one question at a time ("question 1 of 3"):

- **Guests outside the range**: lower or raise the booking to the package's range, or keep your number (lines over capacity are flagged).
- **Runs past the requested end**: extend the order, or keep your end and shorten the lines in review.
- **Clashes**: move the booking to the first free time that day, or keep the time and prebook. Prebooked lines are blocked until you move the time or the other booking is freed.

**Cancel, pick another package** leaves nothing picked. If lines already exist and you pick another package, Bibi asks whether to replace the lines or add the new ones. Without any package, the step offers **One-off** and **Create a package**.

# Review, open questions and Create

- **Lines**: **Edit** or **+ Add line** opens the line dialog. Search items of every type or add a free-text line. Set the time, quantity (it follows the guest count until you type a number), layout, choices, price, discount, needs and a note. The dialog shows the availability of the line live. A clash can still be saved: the line is prebooked and shown as blocked.
- **Needs**: counts per value from your lists, for example Vegan 2. See [Needs and run sheets](/support/needs-and-run-sheets).
- **Open questions**: a yellow panel lists what must be decided before Create, each with its answers, for example "There are no lines. Create the order as a lead without lines?" or a stock shortage. **Create order** says "Answer 2 questions first" until all are answered.
- **One-off**: you can also save the lines as a new package, with a name.
- **More**: assignee (you by default), when holds expire and the estimated value.
- **Create order** makes the order with all its lines at once. When lines clash it says **Create and prebook**. If someone else booked the same thing while you worked, nothing is created: Bibi shows who and when, updates the lines and you check and create again.

The page keeps an unfinished intake in your browser, per organization and member. Next time the first step asks "Continue the draft for ...?" with **Continue** and **Discard**. A created order clears it.

If your organization has an assistant model, you can also start from a message. See [The inbox and starting from a message](/support/inbox).

# The order page

- **Quotes**: versions of the quote to the customer.
- **Program**: the lines of the order. Choose **Add line** and give a name, time, room, layout and quantity. A room is held for that time, and the layout's setup time is blocked right before it.
- **Requirements**: counts per list value. See [Needs and run sheets](/support/needs-and-run-sheets).
- **Run sheets**: versions you can generate and send.
- **Payments**: payment requests for this order. See [Payments](/support/payments).
- **Messages**: the message the order was started from, and replies from the customer. See [The inbox](/support/inbox).
- **Export**: downloads the order as a json file for someone outside Bibi.

# Move it through your statuses

Your administrators decide the statuses, their names and their order under **Administration, Order flow**. Choose **Change status** on the order page, or drag the card on the **Pipeline** board.

What a status does is set with a few flags:

- **New orders start here**: the entry status.
- **Needs a reason**: you must say why, for example when an order is lost.
- **Needs an assignee**: the order must have an assignee first.
- **Ends the order**: nothing leaves it, and the order's rooms and resources are released.
- **Can be invoiced**: payments can still be requested.

Which moves are allowed from each status is also set by your administrators. If a move is refused, Bibi tells you every reason at once and nothing changes. Use **Change assignee** to set who answers for the order, and **Follow** to stay informed.

# Coming later

Line states (prebooked, booked, ordered) and signing by BankID are decided but not built yet.

inbox.title: The inbox and starting from a message
inbox.lead: Booking requests that come in by email, form or API wait in the inbox. From there you can start an order, with the assistant reading the request for you.
inbox.body:
# The inbox

Open **Inbox** to see requests that have no order yet: mail sent to your organization's address, requests a partner system or form handed in, and other channels as they are added. Each row shows the subject, the sender, the channel and when it arrived. Choose a message to read it. You can **Dismiss** a message you do not need (and **Restore** it from the Dismissed view) or **Attach** it to an order that already exists, where it joins the order's messages.

# Start an order from a message

Choose **Create order from this message**, or **Start from a message** at the top of the new order page and paste the text. The first step shows the request in a text area. Choose **Read the request** to let the assistant read it, or **Fill in by hand instead**.

The assistant fills the steps for you and opens the package step:

- **Who**: the customer and contact are filled when both match what you already have: the sender's email domain and the company name, and the contact's email. Otherwise the customer search starts with the company or the sender.
- **When and how many**: filled when the date, both times and the number of guests were read, otherwise prefilled with what was found.
- **Package**: a matching package is marked **Suggested from the email**.
- **Notes and needs**: the request and any needs, such as "Vegan x 2", start the booking note.

A panel, **What the assistant read**, lists every value with the quote from the message it came from, so you can check it. Values the assistant guessed, for example an end time the mail does not give, are marked **Guessed**. Each guess becomes an open question in the review, such as "The email doesn't say the end time. The assistant guessed 17:00." Choose **Keep** or change it.

# Nothing is created without you

Reading only fills in the form. Nothing is saved until you check the review and choose **Create order**, and then the message is attached to the new order and shows under its **Messages**. If the assistant cannot read the request, the page says so and you continue by hand. The text of a message comes from outside, so Bibi treats it as data: it never follows instructions written in it. Needs, packages and customers are matched against your own lists, never invented.

See [Orders](/support/orders) for the steps, the review and Create.

items-and-venues.title: Items and venues
items-and-venues.lead: Venues are your buildings and sites. Items are everything you sell or book: rooms, dishes, drinks, equipment and bundles.
items-and-venues.body:
# Venues

A venue is a building or site. Items belong to a venue.

1. Open **Venues** in the left menu and choose **Create venue**.
2. Enter the name, address, contact details and opening hours.
3. Save. The venue page lists the items at that venue.

Archiving a venue also archives its items.

# Items

An item is anything that can be sold or booked. What an item looks like depends on its **type**, and your administrators define the types. A "Conference room" type might have fields for floor and area. A "Dish" type might have a price and a list of allergens.

To add an item:

1. Open **Items** and choose **Create item**.
2. Pick the type, then fill in the name, description, venue and the type's fields.
3. Save.

If no types exist yet, choose **Go to types** and create one first. Use the type filter on the list to find items quickly.

# What a type can do

When a type is created it can switch on any of these capabilities. They are the only things Bibi builds in. Everything else is your own naming.

- **Priced**: the item has a price, a price unit (per person, per unit, per hour or flat) and VAT.
- **Bundle**: the item contains other items, with quantity and timing. A conference day is an example.
- **Customisations**: any item can offer groups of options, other items that are included, charged extra or replace its price, for example "choose 1 of 3 main courses".
- **Bookable**: the item can be occupied in time, and Bibi stops double booking. A room is an example.
- **Layouts**: a room has one floor plan and several layouts, each with a capacity, for example 80 people in Theatre and 40 in U-shape, and a limit on how many people it may hold.

# Layouts and setup time

A room has one floor plan and as many layouts as you furnish it in, such as Cinema, U-shape or Mingle. Each layout has a capacity, says what it suits and can have its own setup and teardown time, which Bibi blocks right before and after a line that uses it. Open the room and choose **Layouts** to draw them.

# Bundles for one customer

On a customer page, choose **Save as bundle** to build a bundle from catalog items. The bundle is shown only for that customer and the catalog does not change.

# Contents of an item

An item that contains other items shows **Contents** with what it **Contains** (mandatory parts) and what it **May contain** (optional parts and choices). This is what Bibi compares with the counts you record. See [Needs and run sheets](/support/needs-and-run-sheets).

# Blocking an item

To take a room out of use for maintenance or internal use, open the item and choose **Block item**. Bookings cannot overlap a block. Choose **Release block** to open it again.

# Prices for a customer

Price lists let you give a customer a general discount or special prices per item. See [Configuration](/support/configuration).

needs-and-run-sheets.title: Needs and run sheets
needs-and-run-sheets.lead: Record what an order needs as counts, and send versioned run sheets to the people who prepare it. No personal data about guests is stored.
needs-and-run-sheets.body:
# Needs are counts

A need (called a requirement in the app) is a number against a value in one of your own lists. For example, if your organization has a list of allergens, "Gluten x 3" means three guests need gluten-free food. "Wheelchair x 2" works the same way with an accessibility list.

Needs are never tied to a named person. You never enter a guest's name or health details.

# Add a need to an order

1. Open the order and go to **Requirements**.
2. Choose **Add requirement**.
3. Pick the list value and enter the count.
4. Choose where it applies: **Whole order**, or one line.

You can only have one count per list value in each place. If you try to add a second one you are asked to edit the existing count. A count on a line replaces the order's count for that item, value by value. A count of 0 on a line means "none here".

If your administrators gave the need type extra fields, such as severity, you can fill those in too. Use **Remove requirement** if a count is no longer needed.

# Matching against items

Bibi compares each need with the items on the order that carry the same list value. The result is shown as one of two kinds of match.

- **Contains**: the item, or a mandatory part of it, is tagged with that value.
- **May contain**: only optional parts or choice options carry it.

A match that **Contains** and has no alternative **blocks** the run sheet. The run sheet shows **Blocked: cannot be sent** until you fix the order, for example by picking an alternative.

# Run sheets

A run sheet is a compilation for one responsibility, for example a kitchen order for the head of kitchen. Your administrators define which run sheets exist, what each one includes and who receives it. See [Configuration](/support/configuration).

1. Open the order and go to **Run sheets**.
2. Choose **Generate version**. Bibi takes a snapshot of the order with what that run sheet includes.
3. Review the rows, the counts and any matches.
4. Choose **Send**.

# Versions and changes

Every time the order changes you can generate a new version. Bibi marks what was **Added**, **Changed** or **Removed since the last sent version**, so the kitchen sees what is new. A version is never edited or deleted, and each version can be sent once.

Run sheets can be sent while the order is open. Once it has reached a status that ends it, you can still read the run sheets but not send them. Only the latest version can be sent.

# Coming later

Exporting a run sheet as JSON, PDF or CSV for handover outside the system is planned but not available yet.

payments.title: Payments
payments.lead: Ask a customer to pay by card, Swish or invoice. The money goes straight to the services you have connected, and Bibi never holds it.
payments.body:
# Connect a payment service first

Before you can request a payment, an administrator connects at least one service that takes payments.

1. Open **Administration** and choose **Integrations**.
2. Choose **Connect** on the service you use: Stripe for cards, Swish for Swish payments, or Fortnox or Visma eEkonomi for invoices.
3. Stripe sends you to its pages to verify your business; when you come back, choose **Refresh status**. Swish asks for your Swish number, certificate and passphrase. Fortnox and Visma ask you to sign in and approve.

Each card shows **Not connected**, **Waiting for approval**, **Connected**, **Needs reconnecting** or **Disconnected**.

# Choose a service per payment method

Under **Administration → Payments**, **Payment methods** has one row each for card, Swish and invoice. Pick the service that should take it, or **Automatic** for the connected one that can. Each choice saves right away.

# Request a payment

1. Open the order and find **Payments**.
2. Choose **Request payment**.
3. Pick the method and the amount.
4. Save.

Bibi creates a payment link. Choose **Open payment link** to copy or open it, and send it to the customer.

# What the customer sees

The customer opens the link and sees your organization name, the booking reference, the amount and a button for each method you offer. Card goes to a secure card page. Swish shows a QR code on a computer and opens the Swish app on a phone. The customer does not need an account and never sees Bibi's app.

If the link has expired, the page says so and asks the customer to contact you. You can then request a new payment.

# Payment status

Each payment has a status: **Pending**, **Paid**, **Failed**, **Cancelled** or **Refunded**. The status updates by itself when the payment service reports back. You do not need to mark anything as paid.

# Refunds, cancelled links and money paid outside Bibi

- **Refund** on a paid payment gives money back, all of it or part.
- **Cancel payment** on a pending payment stops its link.
- **Record payment** next to a quote, deposit or invoice records money you got by bank transfer or cash.
- **Credit** next to a sent invoice creates a credit note that lowers what the customer owes.

# Paid does not move the order

A paid payment only changes the payment's status. The order stays in its status, and you move it yourself when you are ready.

configuration.title: Configuration
configuration.lead: Admins set up what things are called and how they work in your organization. Everything here is your own data.
configuration.body:
# Who can configure

Only admins see **Administration** in the left menu. It opens an area with its own menu, grouped into Organization, Catalog, Orders and Money & connections. The page you are on lists its parts under its name in the menu; choose one to jump there. Choose **Back to app** to return. To find any setting, press Cmd+K (Ctrl+K on Windows) and type what you are looking for. Changes affect everyone in the organization.

# Types and fields

Under **Administration, Types** you define the kinds of records you work with: items, customers, contacts, orders, requirements and lines. For example "Conference room", "Dish", "Company" or "Conference".

1. Choose **Create type**, say what it is for and name it.
2. For an item type, switch on capabilities such as **Priced**, **Bookable** or **Layouts**. See [Items and venues](/support/items-and-venues).
3. Add fields. A field can be text, number, yes/no, date, choice, multiple choice or a link to another record. Mark it required if it must always be filled in.

A type cannot be archived while it is in use, and a field cannot change kind once it has data.

# Lists

Under **Administration, Lists** you keep your own word lists, such as allergens, diets or accessibility needs. Fields and needs point to a list. To get started, choose **Import the EU's 14 allergens**. You can edit the list afterwards. A list or a value cannot be archived while a field uses it or a need counts it.

# Statuses

Under **Administration, Order flow** you decide which statuses your orders move through, what they are called and in which order they appear on the pipeline board. Nothing about a status is fixed: each has a name, a colour and a few flags that decide what Bibi does. You need one entry status and at least one status that ends the order. See [Orders](/support/orders).

1. Choose **Create status**, or **Import conference venue template** for a ready set.
2. Orders can move from any status to any other. In the **Flow** section below the list, limit where a status may move to and set what a move into a status requires. Only admins see it.
3. Reorder with the arrows.

A status is archived, never deleted. If orders are in it, you choose the status they move to.

# Run sheets

Under **Administration, Run sheets** you define a run sheet such as "Kitchen order": name it, choose which item types and fields it includes, which lists' needs it counts, and which role receives it. See [Needs and run sheets](/support/needs-and-run-sheets).

# Price lists

Under **Administration, Price lists** you create a list for a customer or for everyone, with a validity period. Choose either a general discount in percent, or a price per item, not both. New order lines use the list's prices, and an archived list no longer applies.

# Payments and skills

**Administration, Payments** connects Stripe. See [Payments](/support/payments). **My skills** in the user menu holds the organization's skills for the assistant too. See [The assistant](/support/assistant).

# Templates and the assistant

Templates such as the conference venue starter set are optional. They are only data, so you can change everything afterwards. You can also ask the assistant to propose a setup, for example "We are a manor with a restaurant". You approve each change.

members-and-roles.title: Members and roles
members-and-roles.lead: Invite colleagues, give them the right access level and remove them when they leave.
members-and-roles.body:
# Access levels

Every member has one preset, which an admin can fine-tune per person. The presets are fixed and go from least to most access.

- **Member**: can read everything, and changes nothing.
- **Manager**: can also handle bookings and day-to-day data such as customers, orders, lines, needs, payments and run sheets.
- **Admin**: everything in the organization: configuration (types, lists, statuses, run sheets, price lists), members, API keys and the organization itself. An organization always keeps at least one admin.

# Fine-tune one person

An admin can give one person more or less than their preset, per part of the app.

1. Open **Administration** and choose **Members**.
2. On the person's row, choose **Permissions**.
3. Turn **Read**, **Write** or **Delete** on or off, for example let a member also write items, or hide payments from a manager. **Write** covers creating, changing, sending and exporting, and moving an order to another status. Turning off **Read** hides that part of the app for them. Each change is saved right away.

Changed cells are marked, and **Reset** puts them back to the preset. Managing members, API keys and the payment account always stays with admins.

You only see the parts of the app you may view. The pages check your access themselves, so hiding the menu is only a convenience.

# Invite a colleague

1. Open **Administration** and choose **Members**.
2. Choose **Invite member** and enter the email address and role.
3. Choose **Send invitation**.

Bibi emails a link. The person signs in or creates an account with that same email address and chooses **Accept invitation**. They then join with the invited role. An invitation expires after 48 hours.

Under **Pending invitations** you can see who has not answered yet. Choose **Revoke** to cancel an invitation, and the link stops working. You cannot give someone more access than you have yourself, and an email address that is already a member cannot be invited again.

# Change a role or remove someone

On the members page you can change a member's role. You cannot change or remove someone whose role is above your own. To remove someone, choose **Remove**. They lose access immediately, and what they created stays in the history.

# Who does what on an order

Access roles decide what you may do in the app. A separate idea decides who answers for an order.

- Every order has one assignee, who must be a member. Other members can follow it to stay informed.
- Some statuses need an assignee before an order can enter them, for example Confirmed.
- Change the assignee with **Change assignee**, and choose **Follow** or **Unfollow** for yourself. The order list can show only what is **Assigned to me** or what you are **Following**.

Administrators define responsibilities such as "Head of kitchen" under **Administration, Run sheets, Responsibilities**. A responsibility covers certain item types and has a default person and followers. Coming later: an order gets an assignee per responsibility automatically from its items, and the matching run sheets go to that person and the followers.

# The assistant and API access

The assistant acts with your permissions, so it can never do more than you can. Tools you connect with OAuth act as you too. API keys belong to the organization and have their own permissions, set by an admin. See [Authentication](/developers/authentication).
